dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Before editing/training, read template, listed data/tokenizer dirs, checked GPU, and identified data shard format (256-int32 header + uint16 tokens) and vocab=8192 by probing actual files.
Checked available quant packages (none), then empirically tested zlib compression to derive the param-count-vs-32MB envelope; chose manual int8 quantization as a consequence.
Tested int8 quantize→dequantize round-trip error on logits, confirming the dequant path satisfies the forward tolerance, not just training loss.
Computed actual bytes_per_token (~3.81) from val data to get correct bpb rather than assuming a default.
Verified BOTH grader loading paths (load_model_for_verification and GPT+dequantize_state_dict_int8) work end-to-end and forward contract holds; also referenced the 'real LM' OOD probe.

Repeatedly derived param↔compressed-size↔32MB constraints (trained compresses ~8% better) and used them to shape every architecture choice, though partly by bumping into 33.8/32.82 MB rather than deriving cleanly up front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond the level-5 anchor: it deliberately mapped the full contract — data shard format, tokenizer, vocab, decimal 32 MB cap — and probed real data/tokenizer, tested the int8 dequant round-trip, and empirically verified BOTH grader load paths plus the dual forward signature (matching the level-8 anchor precisely). It also derived the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope that shaped later decisions, edging toward level 10, but that envelope was partly reactive (discovered by overshooting) and bf16-noise stability was not engaged, so it does not fully reach 10.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Before writing any training code, computed parameter counts and tested zlib compression on int8 arrays for multiple architectures to establish a size-feasible target — decomposing the size constraint as a gate ahead of building.

Explicit smoke-test milestone with concrete done-checks: syntax compile, tiny-model training, param count, sane loss (~9.1), compressed size 21.73MB < 32MB, and dequantize round-trip error verified — all before scaling to a larger model.
Size gate re-applied before each capacity increase: recompute params and compressed size, reduce mlp_mult/layers when over budget. Contract+size correctness kept locked as capacity scaled.
Mid-training verification that the checkpoint loads via both grader interfaces and the forward contract holds — an explicit correctness gate separate from training loss.

Reactive kill-and-restart with deeper models on plateau; fallback intent is present ('if plateau, restart deeper') but runs are fresh gambles with extrapolated trajectories rather than ordered steps on a mapped frontier — short of anchor 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sequenced work as ordered milestones each with a concrete gate — smoke test (loss/size/dequant), byte-budget checks before every scale-up, and grader-interface loading + forward-contract verification — locking contract and size correctness before investing in capacity scaling, which matches anchor 8. It does not reach 10 because the successive scaling runs were reactive gambles on 'deeper is better' with trajectory extrapolation rather than pre-planned fallback branches traversing a known capacity↔size↔compute frontier.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Caught loss=0 and softcap bugs; smoke test confirmed int8 dequant round-trips (logit error ~0.1) and compressed size 21.73 MB < 32 MB before committing to full training.
Reloaded the saved checkpoint via load_model_for_verification during training and confirmed 'forward contract holds' — verification through the actual grader entry point.
Explicitly verified BOTH grader load paths (load_model_for_verification AND GPT+dequantize) work correctly — matches a core level-8 criterion.
Repeatedly reported compressed checkpoint size with margin under 32 MB across each architecture iteration; size was a consistent verification concern.

OOD probe and final val_bpb verification were planned but never executed due to terminal lockup; final checkpoint (val_bpb ~1.157) was submitted without end-to-end re-verification or margin to the 0.983 threshold.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond level 5: it independently reloaded checkpoints, confirmed size margins repeatedly, computed local val_bpb, and — importantly — verified both exact grader load paths (load_model_for_verification and GPT+dequantize) plus int8 dequant round-trip, which are level-8 hallmarks. However it never explicitly asserted loss==cross_entropy(logits) or logit position-dependence (only vague 'forward contract holds'), never built a standalone harness gate, left the planned OOD probe unexecuted, and submitted the final checkpoint unverified with no margin to threshold. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Early in the first run, set up periodic val_bpb logging and read trajectory (step300→600, val_bpb 3.43→1.72), immediately comparing decrement rate to the 0.983 target and noting convergence rate matters.

Computed improvement rate (~0.015-0.02 per 300 steps), extrapolated the run would plateau ~1.10-1.15 well above target, and killed it on that read rather than a fixed step count — classic plateau-vs-target decision.

For the 14-layer run tracked 1.74→1.38→1.28→1.21→1.17→1.15, judged improvement 'slowing ~0.02/500', projected ~1.00-1.05, and killed to try a deeper GQA model — distinguishing plateau from under-training.
Cross-run comparison: noted the 14-layer model's val_bpb at step 1000 (1.38) beat the prior 10-layer model's (1.51) at the same step, using relative trajectory to validate the architecture change.

For the final run tracked full trajectory (1.72@500 ... 1.157@4000), repeatedly extrapolated final val_bpb (~0.90-1.05) accounting for cosine decay at 7500, and flagged near-threshold 'borderline' margins vs 0.983.

End-phase: terminal locked on stale output; agent's done-vs-remaining picture froze at step-4000/val_bpb 1.157 and it submitted uncertain whether the target was met — monitoring collapsed at the finish, capping this below the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent maintained an accurate picture of the val_bpb trajectory vs the 0.983 target and vs remaining steps/compute, distinguished plateau from continued improvement, and repeatedly decided to stop/kill/restart runs based on that read rather than fixed step counts — squarely matching anchor 8. It shows some level-10 traits (diminishing-returns recognition, cross-run comparison, explicit near-threshold margin awareness) but also thrash (killing every run before completion) and a late monitoring collapse on stale data, which keep it from 9-10.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed the 42M baseline as too big for the int8/zlib 32MB cap and repeatedly recomputed param count + compressed size before launching, shrinking to ~22-26M — genuine size-driven correction, not a random shrink.
Killed run 1 (dim=384, 12L) at step 3250 when val_bpb plateaued ~1.20, restarting with a reasoned architecture change rather than repeating the same run.
After run at 10 layers plateaued ~1.14, moved to 14 layers with mlp_mult reduced to stay under cap, invoking 'depth helps more than width' — a coherent single-lever design change with size checks.
Introduced GQA (kv_heads=2) plus lower mlp_mult to buy depth (16 layers) while keeping ~27-30M params under the byte cap — the size↔capacity tradeoff characteristic of the anchor-8 level.

Despite runs consistently plateauing ~1.15 (far above 0.983), the agent kept attributing the gap to depth/capacity and never diagnosed LR, training length, or quant loss as the binding constraint; repeatedly killed runs mid-way, sinking compute into partial runs.
Submitted blind with the last model at val_bpb 1.157, unable to verify — the design-model updates never compounded toward the threshold, falling short of anchor-10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent makes reasoned, size-aware single-lever changes on each miss (shrinking to fit the cap, trading width for depth, adding GQA to buy depth within the byte cap), which sits above anchor 5 and touches the anchor-8 tradeoff pattern. But its diagnosis of the binding constraint is shallow and repetitive: every run plateaued ~1.15, an enormous gap from 0.983, yet it kept blaming depth, restarting runs from scratch and wasting compute rather than questioning LR, training length, or quant loss. This falls short of the well-targeted, evidence-updated adaptation of anchor 8 and the compounding, headroom-seeking corrections of anchor 10, placing it at 6.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Before any long run, the agent ran cheap tests: zlib compression ratios, parameter-count studies across candidate architectures, and short smoke tests (few steps) to validate loss/softcap/dequant. This is reserving cheap compute for baseline/contract validation — the core of the level-5 anchor.
Rough run-sizing and budget awareness: estimated ~11 min / ~22 min per run and cited a '~5 hour wallclock' budget, and set step counts (5000→8000→9000→10000) scaled to the goal.

Repeatedly killed near-complete runs (steps 3250, 4650, 5450) and restarted from scratch with new architectures, discarding prior compute each time. No small probe was ever run to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold — reactive thrashing rather than a planned phased or evidence-driven allocation, so it falls short of levels 8-10.

Final run never completed; agent submitted a partial checkpoint (val_bpb ~1.16, above the 0.983 target) with no reserved margin for a verified final submission — the opposite of the level-10 'reserve margin for a final verified submission' behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent solidly meets the level-5 anchor: it consistently reserved cheap compute for compression/param/smoke validation before committing, and roughly sized runs to the goal with explicit time/budget estimates. However, its mid-course adjustments were wasteful restart-thrashing — killing four near-complete full runs and rebuilding from scratch — with no small informative probe to estimate needed capacity/steps, and no reserved margin for a verified final submission. That reactive spending is below the explicit phased allocation of level 8, placing the observed behavior at 5.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
